newsitem.title: FRANCE: French fourth-quarter GDP edges up 0.2 percent.
newsitem.headline: French fourth-quarter GDP edges up 0.2 percent.

text.p: France's gross domestic product rose 0.2 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 from the previous quarter, restrained by a drop in consumer spending, national statistics institute INSEE said on Thursday.
The rise was slightly higher than economists' expectations, predicting no growth for the quarter, but they said it was offset by a slight downward revision to third quarter GDP growth.
Third-quarter GDP growth was revised to 0.8 percent from the 0.9 percent initially reported.
INSEE also said that full-year growth was 1.3 percent, in line with the government's official forecast.

The government, which needs stronger growth this year to fulfil its plans to reduce the public deficit in preparation for European monetary union, says it expects growth this year of at least 2.3 percent.
INSEE said that in the fourth quarter, imports rose 1.3 percent but a 1.1 percent rise in exports cancelled most of that out and INSEE said trade's overall contribution to GDP was slightly negative.

Consumer spending, which dropped 0.5 percent, subtracted 0.3 percent from fourth-quarter growth, while investment was a mild positive for the quarter. Fourth-quarter growth was restrained, by less than a quarter of a percentage point, by the impact from the number of working days effect, INSEE added.
Stock-building contributed 0.4 percent growth to the fourth quarter while it subtracted 0.6 percent from full-year GDP growth.
